name: Elevate at Aurora
award: 2022 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: Elevate at Aurora is a 137-apartment affordable community at 1671 Altura Boulevard, about a mile east of the Anschutz Medical Campus, built by Columbia Ventures on land owned by Living Hope Community Church together with a community building for the workforce nonprofit CrossPurpose; it won $2,689,571 a year in federal 4% credit and $1,000,000 in state credit in CHFA's 2022 Round Two.
why_it_matters: It pairs income-restricted housing from 30% to 70% of AMI with an on-site career training center on church land, financed with a church/foundation-funded community facility kept off the housing budget through a triple-net lease, a model for faith-land and workforce partnerships.

status.label: Completed: certificates of occupancy dated 2026-03-16
status.detail: Aurora issued permits for the four apartment buildings (137 units) on 2023-10-19 and for the clubhouse/community building on 2023-10-05; the city's certificate of occupancy layer shows COs dated 2026-03-16 for all five addresses. No placed-in-service or 8609 record or official opening announcement was found.

next_step: Watch for a grand opening or lease-up announcement and CHFA records showing the placed-in-service year.

key_numbers.meaning: 7 at 30% AMI, 7 at 40%, 34 at 50%, 55 at 60% and 34 at 70%; studios to three bedrooms.

key_numbers.value: $2,689,571 a year federal 4% credit plus $1,000,000 state credit
key_numbers.meaning: About $26.9M in federal credit over 10 years (inferred from the annual amount).
$30M of tax credit equity (including $5.5M for the state credit) and a $6.3M equity bridge loan; KeyBank also placed $31.245M of bonds as a tax-exempt loan.
All four apartment buildings and the community building.

facts.value: 1671 Altura Boulevard, Aurora 80011; city permits also use 1681 N Altura Blvd and 1672, 1682 and 1692 N Eagle St for the buildings
4.7-acre parcel owned by Living Hope Community Church; platted as Altura Farms Tract 10 Filing 1 (case 2023-3007)
Four three-story walk-up apartment buildings (35, 42, 42 and 18 units) with breezeways, plus a one-story community service facility; surface parking
Rezoned from R-2 to R-4 (high density) with unanimous City Council approval in February 2022
Across from Altura Elementary, near a King Soopers, two blocks from Colfax 15/15L buses and 0.9 mile from the R Line Colfax station; in a Qualified Census Tract
NGBS Bronze, electrification-ready; rooftop solar permits issued 2025

money.note: The applicant report showed a $2,692,042 request.
KeyBank bought it for $5.5M of state credit equity.

Structured as a construction-to-permanent tax-exempt loan placed with a KeyBank capital markets investor; the application planned $16,190,000 of permanent bonds and a $10,867,892 taxable construction loan.
Includes $5.5M of state credit equity and $292,744 of solar tax credit equity; plus a $6.3M equity bridge loan.

money.source: City of Aurora HOME and ARPA
money.note: The application cited $1,750,000 in city HOME and ARPA approvals.
Conditionally committed by Living Hope Community Church, the Gamel Family Trust and the Anschutz Foundation; CrossPurpose said it would invest $3.5M in its space.

background.text: Living Hope Community Church bought the land at a reduced price from a farmer who wanted it to go to a ministry; it sat vacant for about a decade before the church and CrossPurpose brought in partners.

The application planned a 15,250 sq ft community service facility, mainly CrossPurpose's Aurora location, run through a triple-net lease so the housing budget does not depend on it; KeyBank's release says it also houses Living Hope Community Church.

Aurora issued a demolition permit for an existing structure on the site in August 2023; the Phase I found no recognized environmental conditions and an asbestos survey was included in demolition costs.
The application included a cost basis waiver request and expected construction to start in the third quarter of 2023.
The 70% AMI units and the developer's stated Average Income experience suggest an income-averaging set-aside (inferred; not stated in CHFA's description).
No asterisk footnote applies to this row in the award report; its asterisks only key the Type and Target codes.

discrepancies.text: The award report lists $29,295,000 of CHFA bonds, while KeyBank says it placed $31,245,000 of private activity bonds.
The application describes a 15,250 sq ft community service facility, while the Gazette reports CrossPurpose investing in 16,000 sq ft of space.
